label: Madrid Codices I and II
summary: Two Leonardo manuscripts in the Biblioteca Nacional de Espana, Madrid, Mss. 8937 (Madrid I) and 8936 (Madrid II), reported rediscovered in the 1960s.

claims.statement: This legacy record stands for the pair; each codex has its own record (ms-madrid-1, ms-madrid-2) because they differ in shelfmark, size and date.

sources.cite: Facsimile Finder, Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de Espana, MS 8937 and MS 8936.

claims.statement: The codices were reported in 1965 by Jules Piccus of the University of Massachusetts.

sources.cite: New York Review of Books, Leonardo's Notebooks, 12 December 1974 (review of the 1974 Madrid codices edition).

check_in: Reti (ed.), The Madrid Codices, 1974, commentary volume

claims.statement: A 1966 Kunstchronik report on the rediscovered manuscripts; the first draft gives 1966.

sources.cite: Kunstchronik (Heidelberg digital journals), 1966 report on the rediscovered Leonardo manuscripts of the Biblioteca Nacional, Madrid.

check_in: Reti (ed.), The Madrid Codices, 1974, commentary volume

claims.statement: Facsimile sellers say Piccus found them in February 1967 (announced in 1967 in the press).

sources.cite: Facsimile Finder, Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de Espana, MS 8937 and MS 8936.

check_in: Reti (ed.), The Madrid Codices, 1974, commentary volume

claims.statement: The codices are said, circumstantially, to have passed from Pompeo Leoni to Juan de Espina, who refused to sell Leonardo volumes to the Earl of Arundel.

value.text: Spanish royal library by 1712 or before 1830

claims.statement: Wikipedia gives entry to the Biblioteca Real in 1712; a facsimile publisher says before 1830, after binding in red morocco in the eighteenth century.

sources.cite: Facsimile Finder, Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de Espana, MS 8937 and MS 8936.

claims.statement: The Biblioteca Nacional de Espana digitised both codices (reported February 2026) and offers them in the Biblioteca Digital Hispanica; the BNE also runs a Leonardo interactive site.

sources.cite: Euronews, The Madrid Codices: Leonardo da Vinci's treasure trove digitised by Spain's National Library, 20 February 2026.
Biblioteca Nacional de Espana, exhibition leaflet on the Leonardo codices.

check_in: BNE Biblioteca Digital Hispanica record URLs

value.text: Draft: Codex I Milan years, Codex II Florence years

claims.statement: The first draft assigns Codex I to the Milan years and Codex II to Florence; sources seen give c.1493 to 1495 for Codex I and c.1503 to 1505 for Codex II with an earlier part c.1491 to 1493, so Codex II is not wholly Florentine.

sources.cite: University of Virginia NEH Institute site, Madrid Codices.

open_questions: Year of rediscovery: 1965, 1966 or 1967. The draft's 1966 needs checking against Reti 1974 and BNE records.
